# dataexplorer

Explore published border quarantine simulation scenarios from Zachreson
et al. (2022).

This package is intended for public health students exploring how viral
transmissibility (R0) and vaccine efficacy relate to infection pressure
from quarantine breaches.

## Installation

Install the package from GitHub:

``` r

# Run once if devtools is not installed:
install.packages("devtools")

devtools::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-xyx81")
```

Access to the repository is required if it is private.

## Launch the app

``` r

library(dataexplorer)
run_app()
```

Select one or more R0 values and use the slider to set the minimum
vaccine efficacy. The plot, summary and table update together.

The dashed line marks the fixed baseline of 1: R0 = 3 and vaccine
efficacy = 0%. Lower values indicate less infection pressure.

## Data and interpretation

The package includes `quarantine_scenarios`, with 100 scenarios and
three variables:

- `r0`: basic reproduction number, from 1 to 10.
- `vaccine_efficacy`: efficacy against infection, from 0 to 0.9.
- `relative_pressure`: integrated infection pressure relative to the
  fixed baseline.

These are historical simulation results under the study’s assumptions.
The outcome is not an outbreak probability or a current forecast. In the
selected analysis, vaccination reduces susceptibility to infection
without reducing infectiousness in breakthrough cases.

The preparation script is `data-raw/prepare-quarantine-data.R`. It
selects and renames three columns from the authors’ published results
without changing their values.

Sources:

- [Zachreson et al. (2022),
  article](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.abm3624)
- [Supplementary code and data (2021),
  Zenodo](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5802433)

## Select scenarios in R

``` r

selected <- select_scenarios(
  data = quarantine_scenarios,
  r0_values = c(3, 6),
  min_efficacy = 0.5
)

selected
```

This returns the 10 published scenarios with R0 values of 3 or 6 and
vaccine efficacy of at least 50%.
